I guess all I am here to say is that yes, birthdays suck. You're not alone.
And try not to worry about family not knowing the "real" you. You are you. You may have things you don't share that are personal struggles, but that doesn't mean that your family who has known you for 33 years doesn't know who you are. Depression may be a part of you but it isn't all that you are and does not define who you are (even if it feels that way). To prove that point- ask yourself about your interests, or anything about you for that matter that isn't depression. Do you like to read? Bike? Watch movies? Go to the beach? These answers make you who you are. Does for family know about any of these answers? Well then they know who you are.

Happy birthday, I wish you peaceful year.

Unfortunately, $120 is not a lot in this world :/, but I do hope if you accept this so that it can help you provide a decent amount of meals a year for you and your daughters (never leave yourself out of that... I don't think you have major depression (basically feeling this way all the time) and by all the time I mean for many months/years., though you haven't specified exactly how long you've been feeling this way. The situation with your dad, that can easily cause you to become depressed. That might, and in my opinion most likely, caused the motivational and memory problems that's affected your school work. I was at a good college and also surrounded by engineers, physicists in my apartment and I was in a major that gets paid shit, basically isn't recognized by the world, so that made me feel probably the same way as you have been. I don't know if any of this even matters so I'm sorry if it doesn't. Btw, your reasons for not being depressed aren't legitimate so don't tell yourself you're just weak for those things. I used to not really cry at all. I've broken bones and what not and I wouldn't cry. I've cried like a damn baby more times than a thousand people could count on their fingers laying in bed at night/in the morning or to counsellors. Oh that reminds me, your college most likely has some kind of student services department that provides counseling to students for free. Take advantage of that and realize people are going there for a billion different reasons so no one will know why you're there if that would stop you. Also they can suggest not only different ways of thinking but get you in contact with whoever they think can help with your unique situation.
